name: Edit machine-drafted captions and transcripts
what: Claim recorded audio/video files from the contractor queue, correct the imperfect AI-generated transcript/captions against the audio (speakers, punctuation, timing), and submit before the deadline.
requirements: 18+, computer with internet, excellent English grammar/punctuation; pass typing test and sample transcript; pass US background check.
who_pays: 3Play Media pays contractors per project at a per-audio-minute rate, with weekly paychecks via direct deposit.
who_qualifies: 18+ with strong written English; no transcription experience required; must pass the typing test, sample transcript, and (US applicants) a background check.
work_available: Contractors claim jobs from an open queue of entertainment, corporate, and education content. Volume varies by season and time of day; slow periods are common and the queue can be empty.
what_gets_accepted: Submissions must meet 3Play's caption quality rules (accurate words, speaker IDs, punctuation, timing); work that fails quality review is not paid.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No fee to join. Unpaid: ~15-min application, typing test and sample transcript, background check, plus unpaid per-file research of names/terms.
when_cash_arrives: Weekly paycheck via direct deposit for work completed in the prior week, at the per-project per-audio-minute rate.
catches: Effective hourly rate is variable: difficult audio (sports, music, technical subjects, multiple speakers, bad audio) can take far longer than the file rate pays, sometimes dragging the effective rate below target.
Work volume is inconsistent — slow seasons and slow times of day are normal; choosing your hours does not create work when the queue is empty.
Contract activity minimums (e.g., at least one project per month) may apply to keep the contract active.
steps: Open the official contractor application at jobs.3playmedia.com/apply on a computer (about 15 minutes).
Take the typing test and complete the sample transcript.
Watch your email for whether you passed to the next step.
Pass the background check required for US-based applicants.
Log into the contractor dashboard once accepted.
Claim jobs from the open queue and note each deadline.
Edit the machine transcript against the audio and submit before the deadline.
Receive weekly pay via direct deposit for completed work.
ease_note: Editing a machine-generated draft is faster than transcribing from scratch, but poor machine drafts on difficult audio erase the time advantage.

name: Proofread and edit academic and professional documents
what: Edit journal manuscripts, theses, and business documents for academic and professional clients; receive proposals by email (topic, word count, deadline) and accept or decline with one click, or pick jobs from the open market.
requirements: Bachelor's degree minimum (master's or doctorate strongly preferred); prior editing experience; excellent English; reliable internet; consistent ability to meet deadlines; pass the editing assessment.
who_pays: Cambridge Proofreading (Chicago-based editing service) pays editors at an average rate of USD 20-30 per hour, with invoices settled twice a month via Revolut or direct deposit.
who_qualifies: Editors with at least a bachelor's degree and prior editing experience (academic editing, publishing, or university teaching preferred); must pass the editing assessment.
work_available: Job proposals arrive by email with topic, word count, and deadline details; editors accept or decline with one click or browse the open market. Volume varies with client demand.
what_gets_accepted: Edits must meet Cambridge Proofreading's quality-control standards; the QC team reviews work and gives personalized feedback, and consistently poor quality can end the contract.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No fee to join. Unpaid: application and editing assessment, plus unpaid time reviewing and choosing proposals.
when_cash_arrives: Invoices are settled twice a month via Revolut or direct deposit.
catches: Requires a bachelor's degree AND prior editing experience — not a route for total beginners.
The 20-30 USD/hour figure is a stated average, not a guaranteed minimum.
Order volume fluctuates; deadlines on accepted orders are strict.
steps: Go to proofreading.org/about/careers/ and review the editor requirements.
Submit the editor application with your degree and editing background.
Complete the editing assessment/test.
If accepted, set your availability on their calendar.
Receive job proposals by email or browse the open market.
Accept orders that fit your expertise and schedule.
Edit and return documents before each deadline.
Get paid twice monthly via Revolut or direct deposit.
ease_note: Hard gate (degree plus proven editing experience), but fully remote, self-scheduled, and full control over accepted orders.

name: Work from home as a customer service representative
what: Handle inbound/outbound customer interactions by phone, chat, or email on behalf of Concentrix's client companies (retail, financial services, insurance, etc.) as a remote employee.
requirements: 18+, high school diploma or GED, typically 1+ year of customer-service experience, US resident with program-dependent state eligibility, reliable internet, quiet home workspace; pass virtual interview and computer/typing assessment.
who_pays: Concentrix (employer, W-2 model) pays hourly wages with regular employee payroll; paid training and company-provided technology reported on current remote postings.
who_qualifies: 18+, US-based with a quiet workspace; high school diploma or GED; most remote programs require about a year of customer-service experience; must pass the virtual interview and assessment.
work_available: Ongoing hiring across dozens of client programs; exact openings and pay vary by program and by state eligibility. Apply on the official careers portal filtered for work-from-home/virtual.
what_gets_accepted: Pass the application, virtual interview, and assessment; complete training; then meet the assigned client program's quality and schedule standards as an employee.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No fee to join. Unpaid: application, assessment, and interview time. Company provides technology; training is paid per current postings.
when_cash_arrives: Regular employee payroll (biweekly direct deposit); paid training is included.
catches: Most remote programs require prior customer-service experience — not pick-up work for total beginners.
These are structured full-time or part-time employee schedules, not flexible gig shifts.
Remote eligibility depends on your state and the specific client program; pay varies by program (realistic range 15-20/hour).
Hiring takes weeks (apply, interview, assessment, background check, training) before the first paycheck.
steps: Go to jobs.concentrix.com and filter for work-from-home/virtual openings in your state.
Pick a remote customer-service program and check its posted requirements.
Complete the application and the computer/typing assessment.
Do the virtual interview.
Pass the background check.
Complete paid training on the client program's systems.
Start taking customer interactions on your assigned schedule.
Get paid biweekly via direct deposit as an employee.
ease_note: Real remote W-2 jobs with stated hourly pay and paid training, gated by a hiring process and usually prior customer-service experience.

name: Work from home as a customer service consultant (financial services)
what: Handle inbound customer inquiries for a multinational financial-products client: research and resolve basic support issues (address changes, orders, billing/payments/disputes), document all work, and escalate as needed.
requirements: About a year of related customer-service experience or high-volume call-center experience; knowledge of credit/debit industry helpful; strong PC skills; reliable hard-wired internet; quiet, distraction-free workspace. Company provides all equipment.
who_pays: Sutherland (employer) offers competitive pay starting at $18/hour with a generous vacation policy, 401k, and medical/dental/vision benefits; all equipment provided.
who_qualifies: Applicants with roughly a year of related customer-service experience or high-volume call-center experience, strong PC skills, hard-wired internet, and a quiet workspace.
work_available: Active remote opening supporting a financial-services client; center operates 24/7; other programs are posted on Sutherland's careers channels as available.
what_gets_accepted: Pass the application and hiring process; complete training; handle inquiries to the client's quality and customer-service standards.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No fee to join. Unpaid: hiring-process time. Company provides all equipment; you provide reliable hard-wired internet and a quiet workspace.
when_cash_arrives: Regular employee payroll (biweekly direct deposit); benefits and 401k included.
catches: Requires roughly a year of related or call-center experience — not for total beginners.
Financial-services program with industry-specific expectations (credit/debit products, back-office regulations).
Structured schedules in a 24/7 operation, not flexible gig shifts; hiring takes weeks before the first paycheck.
steps: Open the official Sutherland posting and read the requirements.
Submit the application for the remote financial-services representative role.
Complete the interview and any assessments.
Pass the background check.
Receive the company-provided equipment and set up your quiet workspace with hard-wired internet.
Complete training on the client's products and systems.
Start handling inbound customer inquiries on your schedule.
Get paid starting at $18/hour biweekly as an employee.
ease_note: Verified current official posting with stated starting pay and equipment provided; hard gate is the experience requirement.

name: Transcribe student reading assessments
what: Listen to audio recordings of elementary students reading and transcribe reading errors (omissions, repetitions, self-corrections) exactly per Literably's scoring guide; files are paid individually.
requirements: 18+, computer with internet (smartphones/tablets cannot be used); pass the ~30-minute sample task (six training recordings) at about 90%; no experience necessary.
who_pays: Literably pays per audio minute (reported range $0.38-$0.80, average about $0.51 since 2020), which works out to roughly $10-18/hour of work once fast and accurate; beginners earn less while slow.
who_qualifies: 18+ with a computer and internet; no experience necessary; hiring is based solely on passing the sample transcription task.
work_available: Work is available when school-assessment audio is in the queue; volume is seasonal and can be limited. Set your own schedule and score available files.
what_gets_accepted: Files must be scored accurately per the scoring guide (exact marking of stutters, omissions, repetitions — not tidied-up transcripts); inaccurate work is rejected.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No fee to join. Unpaid: the ~30-minute sample task and training-test time; rejected applicants must wait 1 year to reapply.
when_cash_arrives: Paid per completed file; exact payout method and schedule are stated in the current official posting.
catches: The sample task is strict (~90% needed) — most applicants fail the first attempt, and rejected applicants must wait a full year to reapply.
New transcribers earn less per hour while slow and double-checking; earnings rise with speed and accuracy.
File volume is seasonal and can be limited — not a guaranteed full schedule.
steps: Create an account at literably.com/scorer-signup.
Read the transcription instructions at literably.com/instructions carefully.
Score the six training recordings in the sample task (~30 minutes).
Wait for Literably's email with your results.
If accepted, log in and pick up available audio files.
Transcribe reading errors exactly per the scoring guide and submit.
Get paid per completed file per the current official terms.
ease_note: No experience needed but the qualification test is genuinely demanding; seasonal file volume.
